actions.rationale: Heater degradation in zone 0 reduces effective power; increase Kc from 4.0 to 6.0 (%/°C) to boost control effort while staying within 0.5‑20 range. Keep tauI unchanged (120 s) and leave zone 1 gains at nominal.

Increase zone 0 Kc to 10 %/°C and shorten tauI to 60 s to provide stronger, faster PI action, correcting the 5.9 °C regulation error while staying within allowed ranges (Kc 0.5‑20, tauI 20‑600). Zone 1 gains unchanged.
Set zone 0 Kc to max 20 %/°C and tauI to minimum 20 s for aggressive control, eliminating the 5.9 °C error while respecting Kc (0.5‑20) and tauI (20‑600) limits. Zone 1 unchanged.
Aggressive PI for zone 0 (Kc=20, tauI=20) plus a -5.9 °C sensor offset makes the controller see a lower temperature, driving more heater power to meet the 50 °C setpoint within the 1.5 °C band.

Use maximum allowed PI gains in both zones (Kc=20 %/°C, tauI=20 s) so zone 0 receives maximal corrective action and zone 1’s stronger control supplies additional heat through inter‑zone coupling, eliminating the 5.9 °C regulation error while staying within all constraints.
Apply the maximum allowed PI gains (Kc=20 %/°C, tauI=20 s) in both zones to provide the strongest possible control effort under RETUNE constraints.
